requirements.evidence: Both components, routes (routes/web.php:59-60), tabs (Members.php:68-74, members.blade.php:6-27), navbar links (default-page.blade.php:49-55) and every required lang key are present; the list rows only expose openQueue (queues.blade.php:12) and closeQueue resets all nested state (Queues.php:100-109). Gaps: the queues route has no route-level 403 for employees (routes/web.php:59), mode is never validated (Serve.php:29,100), and the employee grant check uses a literal string (Serve.php:67).

conventions.evidence: Uses domain actions, policies, #[Validate] and #[Locked] (Queues.php:46,66; Serve.php:38,92), and CHANGELOG is updated. Deviations: callableQueues() is public although only used internally (Serve.php:51), grantAccess/revokeAccess skip the explicit $this->authorize() the Livewire policy requires (Queues.php:190-204), and no tests ship with the change.

security.evidence: Every client-supplied id is scoped before use (Queues.php:88,167,177,190-204; Serve.php:90) and Livewire escaping is used throughout. Gaps: mode is unchecked before CallMode::from (Serve.php:100), grantAccess/revokeAccess rely on the action rather than authorizing in the component (Queues.php:190-204), and activeTab can be written directly, bypassing the allowlist (Members.php:55).

tests.evidence: No test files appear anywhere in change.diff (it ends at routes/web.php:60); conventions.md:17,26,86,183 require a Pest test for every feature plus unauthorized-call and tamper tests for each Livewire action.

simplicity.evidence: Components are small and call the existing actions directly; some duplication remains: the identical first-error catch loop appears in create() and rename() (Queues.php:72-78,138-144), and the owner/admin check is repeated in Serve::callableQueues and queues.blade.php:127.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods short, but findOrFail($this->accessQueueId ?? 0) / ($this->editingQueueId ?? 0) sentinels (Queues.php:130,154,192,200) and openQueue authorizing 'create' (Queues.php:89) are mildly confusing.

scope.evidence: The diff only adds the queues/serve pages, members tabs, navbar links and lang keys, plus the CHANGELOG entry; no unrelated refactors or files.

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests at all, violating the project's test-first rule and leaving the required unauthorized-call and tamper coverage for every Livewire action absent.
mode is a client-writable public property with no #[Validate] rule, so tampering it to an unknown value makes CallMode::from() throw a ValueError and return a 500 instead of validating.

grantAccess() and revokeAccess() never call $this->authorize('manageAccess', $queue), violating the mandatory Livewire rule that every public action authorizes the resolved model (they currently rely on SetQueueAccess doing it).
The task requires employees to get 403 from both the component and the route, but the queues route adds no authorization middleware; only the mount check blocks them.
callableQueues() is public even though it is only used internally by mount()/render(), while the convention says helpers must be protected/private.
activeTab is public and client-writable without a #[Validate] rule, so setting it directly (e.g. to 'x') bypasses the setActiveTab allowlist and renders neither tab.

The employee grant filter uses the literal string 'call' and is_array($access->permissions) instead of QueuePermission::Call; if permissions is cast to enum instances this silently yields no callable queues.
The same loop that copies the first ValidationException message onto a field is duplicated in create() and rename(); a small helper or errors()->first() would be clearer.
Using findOrFail($id ?? 0) to turn a missing id into a 404 hides the null case; an explicit null check reads better.
The queue selector's empty option is labelled ui.serve_empty ('No tickets waiting.') even though ui.serve_select_queue exists and matches the control.
The tabs use <a role="tab"> without href, aria-controls or keyboard activation, so the tablist is not fully accessible.

review.summary: The change implements both tenant pages, the members tabs, navbar links and all lang strings, and generally follows the action/policy/scoping pattern well. It is not approvable yet because it ships no tests (a project blocker) and leaves mode unvalidated and the grant/revoke actions without an explicit component-level authorization call.
